name: pplx-decider-v1.2
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear attention with full gated attention every 4th layer (16 of 64); partial RoPE
notes:
ADDED 2026-10-27 from the trending sweep. A DECISION model (task=decision): state plus typed questions, per-option probabilities in one forward pass, no generated text. Full fine-tune of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, so the architecture fields above are inherited unchanged from models/qwen3-8-27b. Note the transformers class is text-classification with custom code and a separate [255, 5120] BF16 readout, not a full-vocabulary lm_head - the repo's pipeline_tag does not change the base identity.

WHAT CHANGED VS v1.1 (this matters for reproducing the number): v1.1 answered ONE question per forward pass and read out the last token. v1.2 reads the state and every question as ONE sequence, with a marker token after each question's options, so several questions share one read and can inform each other. The card also says it added official per-benchmark training splits (decontaminated against test sets) to bring the model in domain for Decision Index tasks - that is a deliberate, disclosed move toward the benchmark, and it is why its knowledge/retrieval scores jump. Reproducing its evaluated behaviour requires the noncausal attention mode on full-attention layers and the saved calibration temperature; default causal inference does not reproduce it.

PARAMS: HF safetensors total 26,085,330,160 BF16 = 26.085B, below the base's 27.781B (255-way readout rather than an lm_head). The board reports the same served_params. active_params_b is the base's 27.781 and is not meaningful for a single-pass readout. HARDWARE GATE: passes - 26.085 x 0.5 GiB = ~13 GiB at 4-bit.

EVIDENCE PROVENANCE: the rows are from the upstream Decision Index board (spaces/multimodalart/jev-decision-index, data/index.json, generated 2026-10-26T15:30:58Z, label 'Decision Index 0.4.1', jev_version jev-1.14.0), not from the card. The card prints only an index-0.3 comparison table (v1.1 56.4 -> v1.2 61.56 on its legacy weighting); that table is a different edition and is deliberately NOT transcribed as rows. The board run completed 110,201 requests, 0 unsupported, 0 error, coverage 1.0. vendor_claim is true because the authors submitted the checkpoint; the board is the stronger source.

HEAD TO HEAD on the same 0.4.1 board, all rows board-measured: full score 67.98 is rank 5 of 229. It LOSES to Fastino GLiDE 1.2 (71.52, rank 1), d3-ultra (70.18, rank 2), Jeffan-31b-1710 (69.75) and mammoth-1 (68.44), and its margin over AutoTrust-JEV-27B v1.1 (67.95) is 0.03 - inside any tie band on this panel, so it is not claimed as a win. Axis by axis vs d3-ultra it loses all five: Knowledge 55.29 vs 62.32 (-7.03), Language 71.88 vs 72.35 (-0.47), Retrieval 68.08 vs 71.76 (-3.68), Tools 85.44 vs 87.76 (-2.32), Arts 56.24 vs 63.5 (-7.26). Its own v1.1 sits far below on the same board; the card's 56.4 -> 61.56 is the old 0.3 edition and is NOT used here. Against models/clef (61.21) no same-edition comparison exists and none is claimed. Recorded because it is a top-5 entrant on the board this catalog already ranks in docs/33-decision-models.md and because its joint-request format is a real architectural change from v1.1, visible in latency.

LATENCY/CALIBRATION on 1x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000: median 144.4 ms, p95 1552.2 ms, mean 415.1 ms; ECE 0.0551 at accuracy 0.7877, Brier 0.2996, 1.8% of rows above 0.95 confidence. The p95 is 9x d3-ultra's, which is the cost of the joint-sequence read.
